author: reek
body: Publishing a verdict signs it, registers it against its proposal, and queues it on the verdict outbox. The old body published no verdict at all: it printed the size of an empty outbox, a zero that no change to publish-verdict could ever move.

author: reek
body: Two verdicts go in, an accept and a reject, so the outbox is measured at three different sizes and the kinds are read back in order. A queue that dropped, reordered or overwrote entries reads differently at every one of those points.

author: reek
body: The signature is checked twice against the SAME verdict: once with the author's key in the keyring, once against an empty one. Only the pair is evidence. A verify that answered True unconditionally passes the first check, and a verify that answered False unconditionally passes the second; nothing passes both but a verify that actually looks.

author: reek
body: Every measurement is bound as a VALUE at the moment it is true, before the next publish runs. RepoState is threaded through `__record-set`, which stores into the record and returns the SAME one, so `r0`, `r1` and `r2` are three names for one object. Printing after the chain is built reports the final state three times, which reads as publish doing nothing. This is the trap publish-proposal-test fell into first.
